newsitem.title: THAILAND: Centuries-old barge procession honours Thai king.
newsitem.headline: Centuries-old barge procession honours Thai king.

text.p: More than 2,000 chanting oarsmen braved torrential rains on Thursday to hold a rare, centuries-old Royal Barge Procession to celebrate Thai King Bhumibol Adulyadej's 50th year on the throne.

Dressed in colourful costumes and intricate headgear, the oarsmen in 52 barges chanted traditional songs to the beat of drums as they moved rhythmically down the Chao Phaya River to honour the world's longest-reigning monarch.
After travelling nearly three km (1.8 miles) down the river, the king's barge veered out of control momentarily as the 50 oarsmen apparently battled a strong current.

Several navy rubber boats helped push the ornate royal barge back into formation, and King Bhumibol continued on to Temple of Dawn to perform a traditional ceremony to present robes to Buddhist monks.
The Royal Barge Procession, last held in 1987 in honour of King Bhumibol's 60th birthday, dates back more than 600 years when it was performed to demonstrate the country's naval power.
The 2,082 oarsmen are commissioned naval officers who practised twice a week for the past year to perfect the precise rowing style, which varies in each barge.
Barge processions are held on many auspicious occasions, such as coronations, welcoming ceremonies for honoured guests or to transport important Buddha images.
